source_title: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc. - Form 10-K (Fiscal Year 2020)
publisher_issuer: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc. (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0001411579)
company_context: AMC is the world's largest movie-theater operator. COVID-19 forced mass theater closures and a near-empty 2020 film slate, collapsing revenue and triggering a formal going-concern doubt in mid-2020. AMC avoided bankruptcy through a sequence of debt and equity raises, capped by a 2021 meme-stock-driven equity surge.
macro_context: COVID-19 pandemic forced theater shutdowns and studio release delays; in 2021 a retail-driven meme-stock surge in AMC shares enabled large at-the-market equity issuance at elevated prices.
evidence_summary: AMC posted a 2020 net loss of about $4.59 billion as revenue fell 77.3% to roughly $1.2 billion (from ~$5.5 billion in 2019). In June 2020 it disclosed 'substantial doubt' about its ability to continue as a going concern. To survive, AMC raised roughly $2.2 billion of gross cash from new debt and equity from March 2020, secured over $1 billion of creditor/landlord concessions, raised over $80 million from asset sales, and converted $600 million of notes to equity. In January 2021 it completed an at-the-market equity raise of about $579.8 million and converted $600 million of Silver Lake notes into stock, with the 2021 meme-stock rally enabling further equity issuance that pulled it back from bankruptcy.
owner_decision_context: Facing a formal going-concern doubt and depleting cash, management chose continuous, opportunistic capital raising (debt, then heavily dilutive equity, plus creditor concessions and debt-to-equity conversions) rather than seeking Chapter 11, ultimately exploiting the 2021 retail share-price spike to issue equity on favorable terms.
action_taken: Raised ~$2.2B gross from debt and equity from March 2020, won >$1B of creditor/landlord concessions, sold >$80M of assets, converted $600M of notes to equity, then in January 2021 ran a ~$579.8M ATM equity raise and converted $600M of Silver Lake notes to stock, using the meme-stock rally to fund survival.
outcome_evidence: Despite a ~$4.59B net loss, a 77.3% revenue collapse, and a stated going-concern doubt, AMC raised enough capital to avoid bankruptcy through 2020-2021 and continued operating, confirming severe-distress-but-survival enabled by extraordinary equity access.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov returned 403; figures confirmed verbatim in WebSearch snippets attributed to AMC's FY2020 10-K and corroborating named journalism (Variety, Hollywood Reporter, ABC News, CNBC, Nasdaq): net loss ~$4.59B, revenue down 77.3% to ~$1.2B from ~$5.5B, going-concern doubt (June 2020), ~$2.2B raised, $579.8M January 2021 ATM, $600M Silver Lake conversion. Exact period-end cash balance not separately confirmed and omitted.
directly_stated: AMC reported a 2020 net loss of approximately $4.59 billion
2020 revenue fell 77.3% to approximately $1.2 billion from about $5.5 billion in 2019
In June 2020 AMC disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern
Since March 2020 AMC raised approximately $2.2 billion of gross cash from new debt and equity
AMC secured over $1 billion of creditor/landlord concessions and over $80 million from asset sales, and converted $600 million of notes to equity
In January 2021 AMC completed a ~$579.8 million ATM equity raise and converted $600 million of Silver Lake notes into stock
inferred: The 2021 meme-stock rally was the decisive enabler of survival, giving AMC equity-market access it would not otherwise have had
Without continuous capital raising AMC's going-concern doubt would likely have resolved into bankruptcy
why_useful_for_opsiq: Severe-distress-but-survival case driven by an exogenous shock plus an unusual capital-market lifeline. Tests whether the engine recognizes a formal going-concern condition, prioritizes liquidity/equity access as the phase-correct action, and distinguishes survival enabled by extraordinary (and arguably non-repeatable) equity access from a true operational turnaround.
